summary: Feed s098_single to IDS is degraded: 92.3% of bytes are encrypted vs 60% tolerance, blinding payload inspection. All other visibility checks (duplicates, VLANs, one-way, oversize, drops, overload, truncation, tunnels) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: 92.3% of traffic is TLS/encrypted and is being forwarded opaque to the IDS with no prior decryption at the packet broker. IDS requires cleartext payload for signature matching and exceeds its 60% encrypted tolerance.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot inspect payloads for ~92% of bytes; signatures, exploit detection and file extraction fail, drastically reducing detection coverage despite needing full payload and bidirectional flow.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs cleartext to detect threats. Add selective TLS decryption/visibility (e.g., inline decrypt or out-of-band SSL visibility appliance) before the IDS, or route this encrypted feed to a metadata/encrypted-traffic-analysis tool and send only decrypted/cleartext flows to this IDS.
